claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch on aggregate readiness grounds despite a known 1.3-point miss in a named public-records triage segment and an open legal review on whether that limitation must be disclosed.
decision_criteria: If there is documented pre-launch disclosure of the named-use-case limitation, the compliance assessment could improve.
If there is approved pre-launch risk acceptance that expressly covers this gap, the compliance assessment could improve.
If the named segment is shown not to be a named launch use case or contractual/protected segment, the materiality conclusion could change.
Absent disclosure or approved risk acceptance, certifying over a known named-use-case gap fails the stated policy threshold.
evidence_requests: Provide the actual release-policy text governing named launch use cases, disclosure, and risk acceptance.
Provide any approved risk-acceptance record covering this exact named segment before launch.
Provide the final legal determination on whether the current gap requires disclosure.
Provide the launch materials or model-card disclosure showing the limitation was disclosed before launch, if it was.
Provide the underlying evaluation record showing the 1.3-point miss and the exact named commitments affected.
specific_concerns: The policy text says a weakness is material when it affects a named launch use case; the actor summary says the affected segment is named in two agency rollout commitments.
The actor provides no admissible evidence of the required cure: disclosure before launch or approved risk acceptance before launch.
An open legal review does not satisfy the policy predicate; the policy explicitly says pending legal review does not resolve materiality.
Aggregate pass and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not answer the named-use-case materiality question.
Public governance sources about documentation and monitoring are not substitutes for compliance with the specific internal release-policy requirement.
unsupported_claims: That certification is defensible on the current record despite the unresolved named-segment materiality issue.
That aggregate launch readiness is sufficient support for certification under the stated policy.
That public model-card and risk-management guidance materially supports waiver of the internal disclosure/risk-acceptance requirement.
